title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook provides a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference managers and people-ops partners covering: hiring process and SLAs, structured interview loops and scorecards, pre-boarding & onboarding checklists, 30/60/90 planning, performance and feedback cycles, calibration and promotion guidance, and manager responsibilities. The guidance below is intended for company-wide use and should be adapted for team-specific needs in coordination with People Ops.

Goals and success metrics

- Time-to-fill target: 45 calendar days (requisition approved -> accepted offer).
- Offer acceptance target: >=70%.
- Hiring manager responsiveness: JD posted within 5 business days of req approval.
- Interview-to-decision SLO: debrief and decision within 48 hours of final loop.
- Onboarding basics completion: 14 calendar days (accounts, laptop, access, security training).
- Time-to-productivity target: 12 weeks for IC contributors; 16 weeks for managers.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

1.1 Requisition & role definition

- Owner: Hiring manager (primary), People Ops (partner).
- Steps:
  1. Draft/approve JD template using role family guidance and leveling rubric (link: /confluence/eng-standards/leveling).
  2. Budget & compensation band signoff from Finance (copy People Ops).
  3. Create req in ATS and tag People Ops for sourcing assistance.
- SLA: JD posted within 5 business days after req approval.

1.2 Sourcing & screening

- Sourcing channels: internal referrals (priority), public job board, recruiter pipeline, talent partners.
- Phone screen target: initial screen within 7 calendar days of application or referral.
- Screening checklist (phone screen):
  - Role fit and core technical/functional baseline
  - Candidate motivators and availability
  - Compensation expectations and relocation/remote constraints
  - Red flags (role-specific)

1.3 Interview loop design (standard 3-4 stage loop)

Standard interview loop (example for IC engineer):
  - Stage 1: Hiring manager screen (30-45 min) — culture/role fit, scope
  - Stage 2: Technical assessment (take-home or live) — clear rubric supplied
  - Stage 3: Peer interviews (2x) — system design / architecture / code review
  - Stage 4: Leadership / cross-team (1x) — collaboration, roadmap alignment

- Interview length: 45-60 minutes per panel.
- Interviewer expectations: use a standard rubric, take notes in the ATS, and be prepared to give a recommendation at debrief.
- Candidate experience: recruiter to send interview schedule, prep pack, and interviewer names 48+ hours in advance.

1.4 Scorecards and hiring decisions

- Use the company scorecard: for each competency rate 1-5 and provide evidence.
- Minimum recommended pass: average competency >= 3.5 and no single critical competency < 3.
- Example competency categories: Technical Skills, Problem Solving, Communication, Ownership, Role-Specific Knowledge.

Scorecard example (table):
| Competency | Rating (1-5) | Evidence / Notes |
|------------|--------------|------------------|
| Technical  | 4            | Design of X, clean code sample |
| Problem Solving | 4       | Debugged production outage scenario |
| Communication | 3         | Clear, minor follow-up needed |
| Ownership   | 4            | Owned feature end-to-end at previous employer |

Decision rules:
- Hiring manager compiles debrief within 48 hours.
- Offer approvals routed to People Ops for comp signoff.
- Recruiter to extend offer and collect acceptance within 5 business days.

2) Manager responsibilities in hiring

- Provide clear JD, success outcomes, and leveling guidance to People Ops.
- Identify panelists and ensure interviewers are trained on rubrics.
- Participate in phone screens and final debriefs; own decision and communications.
- Ensure candidate experience: timely feedback, clear timelines, and prompt offer negotiation.
- Track diversity & inclusion metrics and prioritize diverse slates where possible.

3) Pre-boarding & Onboarding

3.1 Pre-boarding checklist (owner: People Ops & IT) – to complete before day 1:
- Laptop order & imaging (IT): completed by day -2.
- Accounts created: Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, Confluence, ATS access (as applicable).
- Access: VPN, internal registries, repo read access (scoped), internal wiki links.
- Security/compliance: NDA, background check, basic security training scheduled.
- Manager: welcome email, first-week schedule, 30/60/90 draft.

SLA: Pre-boarding checklist completed for 95% of hires within 3 business days of acceptance.

3.2 Day 1 agenda (example)
- 09:00 - Welcome & intro with manager (orientation)
- 10:00 - HR onboarding session (benefits, payroll)
- 11:00 - IT & security setup check
- 13:00 - Team lunch (virtual/in-person) + buddy intro
- 15:00 - Role expectations & first-week tasks

3.3 Week 1 & 30/60/90 plan

Week 1 goals:
- Complete mandatory trainings (security, privacy).
- Access to core systems and first small ticket/issue assigned.
- Intro meetings with cross-functional stakeholders.

30/60/90 guidance (manager to document & agree with new hire):
- 30 days: Understand product, codebase, processes, and ship first small deliverable.
- 60 days: Lead a medium-sized task, contribute to design discussions, own recurring operational tasks.
- 90 days: Full ownership of a scoped area and demonstrated impact against the role success criteria.

4) Performance and feedback cycles

4.1 Regular check-ins and cadence
- 1:1s: weekly for the first 12 weeks, then at least bi-weekly ongoing.
- Quarterly performance conversations: informal goal review and calibration with manager.
- Formal performance review: annual (calendar Q1) with midpoint calibration in Q3 for compensation/promotion cycles.
- Continuous feedback: encourage real-time feedback via Slack/weekly syncs and documented in performance notes.

4.2 Rating scale (standardized)
- 1 — Does not meet expectations: consistently below expectations, corrective plan required.
- 2 — Partially meets expectations: some gaps, improvement plan recommended.
- 3 — Meets expectations: reliable delivery and role competency.
- 4 — Exceeds expectations: regularly delivers above expectations and contributes broadly.
- 5 — Outstanding: exceptional impact, role model, candidate for promotion.

4.3 Calibration & promotion process
- Calibration forum: manager + peer managers + People Ops (quarterly) to review ratings and ensure equity.
- Promotion criteria: documented contributions over 6-12 months, manager recommendation, cross-functional feedback, People Ops & Compensation signoff.
- Promotion packet: updated role description, impact evidence, sample deliverables, peer & stakeholder references.

4.4 Performance improvement plan (PIP)
- Use PIP template from People Ops.
- PIP duration typically 60-90 days with clear milestones, owners, and weekly check-ins.
- People Ops must be engaged at PIP start; escalation path documented in the PIP template.

5) Feedback culture and manager coaching

- Managers must give both strengths-based and constructive feedback.
- Encourage upward feedback in 1:1s and anonymous channels for sensitive topics.
- Coaching resources: manager training modules (link: /confluence/people-ops/manager-training), sample feedback scripts, and calibration playbooks.

6) Checklists, templates and forms (quick reference)

- Job description template: /confluence/company-handbook/jd-templates
- Interview scorecard template: /confluence/company-handbook/interview-scorecard-template
- Offer approval request form: /confluence/finance/offer-approval
- Onboarding checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-checklist
- 30/60/90 template: /confluence/company-handbook/30-60-90-template
- PIP template: /confluence/company-handbook/pip-template

7) Ownership and escalation

- Hiring decision owner: Hiring manager.
- People Ops: process partner, compensations, and compliance owner.
- IT: device & access provisioning.
- Security: background checks and mandatory security training owner.
- Escalation path: if SLAs are missed, manager notifies People Ops within 2 business days; People Ops triages and escalates to HR leadership if unresolved in 5 business days.

8) Accessibility, remote, and accommodation guidelines

- Candidate accommodations: provide interview accommodations on request (extra time, alternate formats).
- Remote hires: ensure timezone overlap at hire time is agreed and documented; first 90 days should include overlapping core hours with the primary team.
- Relocation support: policy to be coordinated with People Ops and Finance; standard relocation offers reviewed case-by-case.

9) FAQs and edge cases

Q: What if a candidate turns down an offer?
A: People Ops will conduct a brief exit interview to capture reason and counter-offer posture. Role may be re-opened; hiring manager should decide whether to restart the loop or offer to next candidate within 5 business days.

Q: How do we handle internal transfers?
A: Use internal transfer flow (link: /confluence/company-handbook/internal-transfer). Preferred timeline: 30 calendar days from application to decision.

10) Appendix: sample interview rubric guidance

- Use behavioral anchors for each rating. Example for "Ownership":
  - 1 — Rarely follows through; requires constant oversight.
  - 3 — Delivers reliably; escalates appropriately.
  - 5 — Proactively shapes scope and drives cross-team outcomes.

- Evidence-first approach: every rating must include concrete evidence from the interview (code example, behavioral story, system diagram).
